newsitem.title: USA: Jessica Mitford's son sends pianos to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Jessica Mitford's son sends pianos to Cuba.

text.p: A California piano tuner said on Sunday he was sending a shipment of pianos to Cuba in what he called a tribute to his late mother, the crusading author Jessica Mitford.

Tuner Benjamin Treuhaft, 48, said he planned to travel to Cuba to recondition some of the pianos despite receiving a warning from the U.S. Treasury Department that he could be fined up to $1.3 million and jailed for up to 10 years.

The truckload of 12 used pianos and a ton of piano parts was scheduled to leave San Francisco on Monday on its way to Montreal where the pianos would be put on a ship to Cuba, said Treuhaft, of Berkeley, California.
Most of the pianos were donated and some were sold cheaply, Treuhaft said. They will go to music schools and pianists in Cuba and at least one will be a prize in a competition.
This is the second shipment of pianos to Cuba by Treuhaft's "Send a Piana to Havana" project. The first shipment of 23 pianos arrived there late last year.
Treuhaft said this shipment was a tribute to his late mother. Mitford, famous for her book "The American Way of Death", an indictment of the funeral industry, died in nearby Oakland in July.
After her death, dozens of admirers contributed more than $10,000 in her honour to send the pianos to Cuba.
Treuhaft said "Send a Piana to Havana" was Mitford's "favorite charity and the government's missteps in dealing with the subversive musical project brought her much glee towards the end of her life."

Treuhaft decided to send pianos to Cuba after visiting the country and seeing the bad state of pianos, many of which were pre-embargo American instruments or poor-quality Russian ones. Many were eaten by termites and rusted by the hot salt air and parts were unavailable, he said.
Treuhaft said he had a U.S. Commerce Department license to send pianos to Cuba. But he says the Treasury Department has tried to fine him $10,000 for a 1994 trip to Cuba to tune pianos.

After he told them of his planned return to Cuba, Treuhaft said the Treasury Department sent him a "Cease and Desist" order warning him he could face a heavy fine and jail under the Trading with the Enemy Act.
Under the U.S. embargo on Cuba, Americans may only travel to Cuba for certain educational and humanitarian purposes.
